items.stem: 4 week old term M, exclusively breast-fed, scleral icterus progressing over several weeks, stools fewer and paler, afebrile and well-appearing, enlarged liver, total bilirubin 12.5 mg/dL, ultrasound shows no gallbladder
items.key: High direct bilirubin, high GGT, normal reticulocyte count
items.companion: Biliary atresia: duct destruction raises GGT, and with no hemolysis the reticulocyte count stays normal
items.d1: High direct bilirubin, normal GGT, normal reticulocyte count
items.d2: High direct bilirubin, high GGT, low reticulocyte count
items.lead: Which of the following sets of laboratory findings is most likely in this patient?

items.stem: 6 week old F, jaundiced since 3 weeks of age, pale clay-colored stools, dark urine, hepatomegaly, raised direct bilirubin and GGT, ultrasound with a small gallbladder and a triangular cord sign
items.companion: Biliary atresia: no contrast reaches the bowel; biopsy supports, but cholangiography is the gold standard
items.lead: Which of the following is the gold-standard study to confirm the diagnosis?

items.stem: 7 week old M with acholic stools and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia; intraoperative cholangiogram shows obliterated extrahepatic ducts with no contrast entering the bowel
items.companion: Biliary atresia: Kasai first; most children still need a liver transplant later

notes: UWorld Q2 (biliary atresia) backfilled into neonatal-jaundice. Existing biliary atresia row updated (2 to 8 week window, GGT and gallbladder tells, transplant endpoint); workup table gains a direct-branch group (GGT/ALP/retics with PFIC and HLH branches), an ultrasound row and a liver biopsy row. Three items: source lab-pattern item (key and the two most-chosen distractors, PFIC and HLH), gold-standard confirmation, and Kasai as the next step. Existing 'Kasai before about 60 days' and 'after ultrasound and HIDA' left as is (not in the UWorld explanation; the 60-day figure carries a warning flag elsewhere on the page). The Skip row ('Hepatic ultrasound or serum albumin') is scoped to jaundice under 24 hours, so the new ultrasound row is labeled 'direct branch' to avoid an apparent contradiction. No second vignette added: the brief's vignette is the NBME source and the Part I brief does not require one per question. Ursodiol distractor is standard cholestasis care, not from the UWorld text.
